In "income below poverty level", 27.8 percent of the families in census tract 413 were below poverty level, area 414 had 17 percent below poverty level. The Randolph Community has 22 percent at or below poverty level, and 237 families or 12 percent with public assistance or public welfare income. Included in these computations are 748 persons 65 years or older receiving Social Security income.
Although the Randolph Community is composed of 63 percent renters and 37 percent homeowners, it has long and stable residential roots. Many of the homeowners have lived most of their lives in Randolph, in many cases the home has passed into second generation ownership. According to census information, 58 percent of the residential population have resided at the same address for the last five years.
The Randolph Community is largely comprised of census tracts 413 and 414. A small portion of the community extends into tract 411. The data above was extrapolated from the 1970 census "Block Statistics" and "Income Characteristics of the Population".
b. The socioeconomic character of the Randolph Community is expected to change very little. This conclusion is based on several factors: 
(1) Relocation and redevelopment will be staged to provide home ownership and rental opportunities within the Randolph Community and other areas.
(2) Through relocation payments a number of renters will now be able to become home owners. This should increase the percentage of potential homeowners; during the same period the new homes built in Randolph will automatically be offered first to relocated Randolph residents.
(3) Many families have established stable residential roots within the Randolph Community. It can be expected that many of the existing residents will desire to remain in the Randolph Area as the housing opportunities are competitive with other communities within the city.
